gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns a cutoff-support defect at the PML boundary endpoints that omits the nearest reflected kernel and invalidates the separated-remainder estimate. ISSUE-001 instead diagnoses an overbroad compact-set quantifier and an invalid comparison of unstretched physical fields with PML fields inside the absorbing layer. The shared theorem context does not establish the endpoint-cutoff or reflected-kernel diagnosis.

Both entries identify the computable-field convergence estimate as being asserted for compact sets in all of Ω_R even though the underlying PML-PDE estimate and physical-field comparison are supported only for compact subsets of Ω_p. The prediction explicitly identifies the unsupported PML-region claim and repairs it by restricting K to Ω_p.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The computable-field convergence theorem overclaims uniform compact-set validity in Ω_R by transferring an estimate proved only on compact subsets of the physical domain Ω_p; compact sets intersecting the PML region are not covered by the stated PDE convergence result.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem claims the computable-field estimate for every compact K contained in Ω_R, although the source PDE estimate is stated only for K compactly contained in Ω_p and no argument extends it through the PML region.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the Ω_R quantifier, explains that Ω_R contains the PML layer where the physical and stretched fields differ, notes that the underlying estimate holds only for K compactly contained in Ω_p, and gives the matching restriction repair.
